Wellbeing check-ins as a standing part of supervision

Dress Code and Uniform Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out dress code and uniform standards for staff at Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to
every employee, uniformed and non-uniformed, at every site and Central Support Office.

Policy statement

A consistent, professional appearance supports both practical safety in care delivery and the confidence
people supported and their families place in Alderbridge, and this policy balances that standard with
reasonable accommodation for individual, cultural and religious need.

Definitions

**Uniformed role** a role for which Alderbridge supplies a standard uniform (care staff, kitchen staff,
housekeeping staff). **Non-uniformed role** a role without a supplied uniform, where a general
professional dress standard applies instead. **Uniform allowance** the payment described in the Uniform
Allowance Guidance supporting uniform purchase and replacement.

Roles and responsibilities

**Every uniformed employee** wears the current Alderbridge uniform, clean and in good repair, with an
identity badge visible at all times on shift. **Every non-uniformed employee** dresses in smart,
professional attire appropriate to a care environment. **The registered manager** addresses a dress code
concern directly and promptly, and considers a religious or cultural dress request sensitively.

1. Uniformed staff wear the uniform supplied on commencement of employment, replaced annually or as
needed through the Uniform Allowance Guidance.

2. Non-uniformed staff dress professionally, avoiding clothing that could pose a safety risk, such as
dangling jewellery near care activities.

3. An identity badge is worn visibly at all times while on shift, for both uniformed and non-uniformed roles.

4. Reasonable accommodation is made for religious or cultural dress requirements, provided infection
control and safe working requirements continue to be met.

5. Footwear for care staff is enclosed and non-slip at all times on duty, consistent with the Slips, Trips and
Falls Prevention Procedure.

Uniform and appearance

Where a role requires a uniform, this is provided by Alderbridge and is expected to be worn clean and in good repair; general appearance standards are set out in the Dress and Appearance Guidance.

Whistleblowing

An employee who becomes aware of wrongdoing is encouraged to raise this through the Whistleblowing Policy, which provides a route to raise a concern confidentially and protects an employee who raises a genuine concern in good faith.

Ending employment

An employee wishing to resign provides notice per their own contract; Human Resources conducts an exit process covering the return of Alderbridge property, a final pay calculation, and, where the employee agrees, an exit interview.

Why the wellbeing and benefits summary was added

A staff survey found that many employees were not fully aware of the wellbeing support already available to them, since information was spread across several separate policies each covering only one aspect; this version's consolidated summary, mirroring the same addition made to the Employee Handbook and Terms document, addresses that gap directly.

Probationary period

A new employee typically serves a probationary period set out in their own contract, during which their performance and suitability for the role is assessed through regular informal check-ins with their registered manager; successful completion is confirmed in writing.

Performance management summary

Alderbridge expects every employee to perform their role to a good standard; a performance concern is normally addressed informally in the first instance through supportive conversation and, where needed, a short improvement plan.

Employee recognition

Alderbridge recognises good work through a variety of means, including a simple thank-you from a manager, a mention in a team meeting, or a nomination for an annual staff recognition award.

Travel between sites

An employee occasionally required to travel between Alderbridge sites as part of their role claims travel expenses per the Expenses Policy, and any time spent travelling between sites during a working day is counted as working time.

Social media

An employee is personally responsible for what they post on social media; a post that identifies Alderbridge, a resident, or a colleague is subject to the same standards of conduct and confidentiality that apply at work.

Supporting a member of staff through a multi-agency process

Being the person who first raised a financial abuse concern, or being interviewed as part of an Office of the
Public Guardian or Action Fraud investigation, can be stressful for a member of staff even where they have
done nothing wrong; the registered manager checks in with any staff member directly involved, offers
access to the Employee Assistance Programme, and ensures they are not left feeling isolated once the
matter has moved beyond Alderbridge's own internal process.

How this version's changes were communicated to staff

The introduction of the Office of the Public Guardian and Action Fraud routes was communicated to every
registered manager through a briefing led by the organisation-level Safeguarding Lead, aligned with the
same communication given for the Resident Finances and Appointeeship Policy's own financial abuse
recognition, so staff understood the two documents as a single, consistent picture rather than two
separate, potentially conflicting updates.

resulting from having made a protected disclosure, which is unlawful regardless of the discloser's
employment status or length of service. **Whistleblowing hotline** the confidential, externally hosted
telephone and online reporting service available to every worker in addition to Alderbridge's own internal
routes.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any worker** may raise a concern under this policy, whether or not it relates to their own role or team.
**A line manager or the registered manager** is the normal first point of contact, though a worker
uncomfortable raising it there may go directly to the Alderbridge Quality Lead, HR, or the external
whistleblowing hotline. **The Chief Executive** is informed of any whistleblowing concern that reaches a
certain severity threshold, and receives a summarised, anonymised report of whistleblowing activity twice
a year.

1. Raise the concern with your line manager, the registered manager, HR, the Alderbridge Quality Lead, or
the external whistleblowing hotline — whichever feels most appropriate given the nature and seriousness
of the concern.

2. Provide as much detail as you can (what, when, where, who), though a concern is still taken seriously
even where some detail is missing or the discloser wishes to remain anonymous.

3. The person receiving the concern acknowledges it and explains, so far as appropriate, what will happen
next and roughly what timescale to expect.

4. The concern is investigated by someone independent of the matter, at a level and by a method
proportionate to its seriousness — a minor process concern is handled differently from an allegation of
serious harm.

5. Where a concern also meets the safeguarding threshold, it is escalated under the Safeguarding Adults
Policy in parallel, without waiting for the whistleblowing investigation to conclude first.

6. Feedback on the outcome is given to the discloser so far as confidentiality and any ongoing legal
process allow, even where full detail cannot be shared.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Staff Handbook's uniform standard (specifying what a uniformed role is expected to wear) and the Staff Benefits Guidance (the wider set of benefits this allowance sits alongside).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the increased amounts. A new care assistant starts in March, receiving the increased £55 initial allowance in their first month's pay to purchase their starting uniform, £15 more than the previous version provided; the following April, they receive the increased £35 replacement allowance alongside every other uniformed staff member.

Frequently asked questions

**Why were the allowance amounts increased?** A review of typical uniform costs found the previous amounts had fallen behind actual replacement cost; the increase brings the allowance back in line. **Does a staff member who received the previous £40 initial allowance get the difference backdated?** No, the increase applies from this version's effective date forward, not retrospectively to an allowance already paid.

Closing note

A fair uniform allowance recognises that looking professional has a real cost, and the increase in this version exists to keep that allowance genuinely adequate rather than allowing it to quietly fall behind actual cost over time.

Staff Wellbeing: Support Available

Purpose and scope

These guidance notes set out the wellbeing support available to Alderbridge Care Group staff. They apply to every employee, regardless of length of service or role.

Policy statement

Alderbridge recognises that caring for others sustainably requires staff to be genuinely supported themselves, and treats wellbeing support as a proactive, normal part of working life, not something staff must be in crisis to access.

Definitions

**Employee Assistance Programme (EAP)** a confidential, externally provided counselling and support service available to every employee. **Mental health first aider** a colleague trained to provide an initial supportive conversation and signpost further help. **Wellbeing referral** a manager-initiated referral to occupational health where attendance or performance appears affected by a health condition.

Roles and responsibilities

**Every employee** may access the EAP directly and confidentially at any time. **Line managers** notice and respond supportively to a colleague who appears to be struggling, and make a wellbeing referral where appropriate. **Mental health first aiders**, present at every site, provide an initial, non-clinical supportive conversation.

Access the EAP directly, confidentially and free of charge, for telephone counselling or self-help resources, at any time regardless of the reason.

Speak to your site's mental health first aider, listed on the staff noticeboard, for an initial supportive conversation if you are not sure where else to start.

A manager may make a wellbeing referral to occupational health where attendance or performance appears affected by a health condition, with the employee's consent except where an immediate safeguarding concern requires urgent escalation regardless of consent.

Reasonable adjustments are considered and discussed openly wherever a health condition, physical or mental, affects someone's ability to work as usual.

A difficult personal event (bereavement, relationship breakdown) is met with genuine flexibility and support from line managers, rather than treated purely as an attendance or performance matter.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a wellbeing concern also raises an immediate safety risk to the employee or someone else, the normal consent-based approach to referral is set aside in favour of immediate action and escalation, consistent with how Alderbridge treats any other urgent safety concern.

Local and regional variations

Each site's own mental health first aider list is displayed locally; the underlying support offer (EAP, referral process) is identical everywhere.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Sickness Absence Policy (for how a wellbeing-related absence is managed) and the Flexible Working Policy (for a temporary or permanent adjustment supporting wellbeing).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates proactive support. A line manager at Willow Bank notices a normally engaged community support worker seeming withdrawn over several weeks. Rather than waiting for a performance issue to emerge, the manager has a private, supportive conversation, learns of a difficult personal situation, and together they agree a short period of reduced hours and a referral to the EAP, addressing the underlying difficulty before it affects the employee's wellbeing or work further.

Frequently asked questions

**Is EAP use confidential from my manager?** Yes, entirely — your manager is not told you have used it unless you choose to share that yourself. **Do I need my manager's permission to see a mental health first aider?** No, you can approach one directly and confidentially at any time. **Will using wellbeing support affect how I'm seen at work?** No — Alderbridge actively encourages staff to use the support available, and doing so is never held against anyone in any decision about their role or progression.

Training and competency

Mental health first aiders complete accredited training and refresher sessions; all managers complete training on recognising when a colleague may need support and how to make a wellbeing referral appropriately.

Monitoring and compliance

Anonymised EAP usage data is reviewed periodically by HR to understand overall wellbeing trends across the organisation, never at a level that could identify an individual user.

Uniform Allowance Guidance

*Supersedes the version effective 1 April 2024. Allowance amounts increased.*

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains the uniform allowance available to a staff member in a uniformed role at Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to every site.

Policy statement

A new starter in a uniformed role receives a one-off uniform allowance in their first month's pay, with a smaller replacement allowance paid every April thereafter, supporting a staff member to maintain their uniform to a good standard without cost falling entirely on them.

Definitions

**Uniformed role** a role for which Alderbridge specifies a uniform standard, such as a care assistant or catering role. **Initial allowance** the one-off payment made in a new starter's first month, increased in this version. **Replacement allowance** the smaller annual payment made every April to support ongoing uniform upkeep and replacement, also increased in this version.

1. Pay a new starter in a uniformed role a one-off uniform allowance of £55 in their first month's pay, increased from the previous £40.
2. Pay every staff member in a uniformed role a replacement allowance of £35 every April thereafter, increased from the previous £25.
3. Confirm a staff member's uniformed role status at the point payroll is set up, so the correct, increased allowance is applied from the first pay run.
4. Review the allowance amount periodically to ensure it remains reasonable against actual uniform costs.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Staff Handbook's uniform standard (specifying what a uniformed role is expected to wear) and the Staff Benefits Guidance (the wider set of benefits this allowance sits alongside).

Sickness absence

A staff member reports a sickness absence to their line manager before their shift start time.

Pension

Every eligible staff member is automatically enrolled into the workplace pension scheme per the Pension Scheme Guidance.

Notice periods table

Length of service	Notice period (either party)
During probationary period	1 week
Up to 2 years	1 week per completed year, minimum 1 week
2 years or more	1 week per completed year, up to a statutory maximum

Disciplinary and grievance

A concern about a staff member's conduct or performance is handled per the Disciplinary Procedure, and a staff member's own concern is handled per the Grievance Procedure.

Equality and dignity at work

Alderbridge is committed to equality of opportunity and a workplace free from discrimination, harassment or bullying, per the Equality, Dignity and Respect at Work Policy.

Confidentiality

A staff member handles resident and organisational information confidentially at all times.

Approval and review history

This handbook was approved by the Chief Executive on 1 April 2023, this version took effect 1 July 2026 superseding the earlier version, and is due for review in July 2027.

Why the wellbeing and benefits summary was added

A review found a new starter often did not discover the discount scheme or long service recognition scheme until well into their employment, simply because these were documented separately and not consistently introduced during induction; consolidating a summary directly into this handbook ensures every new starter sees the full picture of what Alderbridge offers from their very first day, alongside the more formal contractual terms.

Uniform and dress code

A uniformed role wears the provided uniform per the Dress and Appearance Guidance, and a non-uniformed role dresses in professional, business-casual attire.

Training and development

Every staff member completes mandatory induction and role-specific training before working unsupervised, tracked through the Mandatory Training Matrix.

Health and safety responsibilities

Every staff member has a personal responsibility to work safely, follow the Health and Safety Policy Full Manual, and report a hazard or concern promptly.
